obligations.subject: phantom fields
obligations.question: Inventory and justify or remove every phantom protocol/type field.
obligations.decision: Retain all 4 phantom fields as-is. Classification: each phantom is a Bombay-derived type-level construction encoding an actor-model law statically (typed message acceptance, creation capability, protocol seats) with zero runtime cost; each is a variance/capability encoding with zero runtime cost and none is removable without losing a static seat. (1) behavior.rs:44 Recipient.message: PhantomData<fn(M)> — contravariant fn-parameter phantom statically coupling a recipient to the message M it accepts without storing or owning M; keeps Recipient Copy regardless of M, avoids drop-check ownership of message data, and lets Delivery<A, M> pair the coupled types (capability encoding: you cannot name a recipient for a message it rejects). (2) behavior.rs:299 Births<C>(PhantomData<fn() -> C>) — covariant return-position phantom encoding the creation capability BirthMode::Child = C at zero size; the fn() -> C form makes Births<C> covariant in C and free of any ownership/drop-check claim over child behaviors. (3) behavior.rs:435 Base.marker: PhantomData<fn(O, Br, E)> — contravariant phantom binding State's three protocol seats (outbound message, birth mode, error) that otherwise appear only in the impl bound; required to avoid E0392 unused-parameter errors while keeping S the sole owned field. (4) fsm.rs:21 Fsm.address: core::marker::PhantomData<A> — owning-position phantom for the address seat A, which Fsm uses only in its Behavior impl associated types (Addr = A, event User<A, M>); required because every struct generic must be used (E0392) and A: Address is Copy so the ownership claim is inert. The checker regex counts exactly these four (three field-form plus the Births tuple-struct special case); count is 4/4 against baseline. No PhantomData exists anywhere else in crates/behavior/src (grep confirms), and no dyn/Any/TypeId accompanies any of them.
